newsitem.title: USA: No more extensions in US/EU meat deadline - Glickman.
newsitem.headline: No more extensions in US/EU meat deadline - Glickman.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Monday there would be "no more extensions" in an April 30 deadline for U.S.-EU agreement on meat inspection rules.
The United States initially set April 15 as the deadline for U.S. retaliation if there was no agreement. It was changed to April 30 because of progress in the talks.
"I will say there will be no more extensions," Glickman told the National Association of Agricultural Journalists meeting.
U.S. and EU negotiations were due to resume Tuesday, Glickman said.
At stake in the "veterinary equivalency" discussions were several hundred million dollars in transatlantic trade in meat, poultry and pet food products.
The EU has implemented new inspection rules that will curb U.S. poultry exports. USDA has said it might retaliate by cutting off EU meat sales to U.S. markets.
